proof.observed: 6 subtests pass: implementer, architect and controller, each in a pod and in a pane. Each asserts PI_CONFIG_FILES is exactly the operator's overlay and the role's own, and reads both keys with `omp config get <key> --json`, requiring each to be on and to equal the same binary's read under HOME and PATH alone.

proof.criterion: A2. A test starts deep-worker from a role session, and the task call returns before the subagent ends. A message sent to the role while the subagent runs is in the role's context at its next model turn, within 30 seconds of the message's arrival. A test of the agent files shows that no agent that Legion ships sets blocking: true.
proof.surface: the real pinned Oh My Pi (/opt/omp/bin/omp, omp/18.12.2) in a role session configured as Legion configures one — the pi-legion package root loaded so agents/ is discovered, a stand-in daemon and a stand-in gateway, real NATS, and no settings overlay of Legion's, so the pin's own --mode rpc defaults decide; and the agent files the plugin ships, read as Oh My Pi reads them
proof.command: cd packages/pi-legion && LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:24222 bun test extensions/legion-background-subagent-omp.test.ts; and cd packages/pi-legion && bun test src/shipped-agents.test.ts
proof.observed: The background-subagent case passes: the subagent's own model request reached the stand-in 19 ms before the parent's first agent_end, and that agent_end came 36 ms before the stand-in released the held request, so the task call returned before the subagent ended; a message published on notifications.agent.<session id> while the request was still held was read 23 ms later in the next model turn, against A2's 30 s bound; and the job's completion woke the role 54 ms after the release, in a turn nothing prompted. The subagent is told from the parent by deep-worker's own system prompt rather than by request order, and `deep` is mapped in modelRoles, without which it would die `No model selected` while the parent still reported the job complete. shipped-agents.test.ts is 26 pass, 0 fail, its `%s declares no blocking field` case over every .md in agents/.
proof.negativeControl: Dropping the `deep` model role times the case out waiting for the subagent's own request — the false green it refuses. Putting `blocking: true` back on deep-worker times it out waiting for the role's request after the task call, the regression it locks; the same literal in agents/oracle.md fails shipped-agents.test.ts by name, and `blocking: false` fails it the same way. Publishing the message after the release instead of during it fails the ordering assertion.

proof.observed: 3 pass in claude-envoy, including `a turn that ends with a background task running earns no reminder, and the task's result starts the next turn`; the Go packages are green. The bridge's two fixtures under internal/claudebridge/testdata are streams measured live from that binary: a background task finishing after a turn starts a fresh turn beginning with a `system`/`init` line and ending with a `result`, and one finishing during a turn emits only `task_updated`, `task_notification` and `background_tasks_changed` and no `result` at all, so it cannot end the daemon's prompt early. proof.command: cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 -run 'TestABackgroundResultsTurnIsNotTheTasksTurn|TestATasksTurnRetiresItOnceWhicheverOfItsEndAndItsResultComesFirst|TestAnAcknowledgementThatLandsInsideItsOwnTurnStillAwaitsItsResult' -v ./internal/supervise/; and cd packages/pi-legion && LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp bun test extensions/legion-phase-stall-omp.test.ts
proof.observed: every case passes; the pi-legion file is 10 pass, 0 fail, including `a turn that ends while the session waits on its own background job gets no reminder, and the job's result wakes it`. Today's code failed A7 before the change, which is why Oh My Pi's prompt_result is now carried as a shimwire frame: measured on the pinned binary, prompt_result arrives after the agent_end of the turn its prompt ran, and a background-result turn ends with none behind it, so the delivery's retire waits for the result rather than for any turn's end.

On the Oh My Pi side, the job started with async false instead of true makes the reminder fire: `Your turn ended with your Legion phase still open`.

trickyParts: A7 failed against the code as it stood, so D8's prompt_result frame was built rather than recorded as unnecessary. Measured on the pinned Oh My Pi: prompt_result arrives after the agent_end of the turn its prompt ran, and a turn a background result starts ends with none behind it. That order is the whole discriminator, and it is why the fix moved the delivery's retire rather than its confirm: the delivery is still confirmed at the turn's start, so ServingRun and ServingAssignment hold through the task's real turn.

Building that test found a second gap the plan did not know of: Oh My Pi's agent_start can reach the daemon before the answer to the prompt that caused it, and the table's row for an acknowledgement that lands inside its own turn was a named ignore, so awaitingResult was never set and the protection did not apply to the faster of the two orderings at all. ackedInTurn records the outstanding prompt there and does nothing else.

R3's second sentence needed no code. Measured against the real Claude Code: a background task that finishes during a turn emits only system lines and no result, so it cannot end the daemon's prompt early. The test for it is a regression guard, and it is the one of the four bridge cases that passes against the unmodified bridge.

The Stop hook's input carries a background_tasks array, which is what lets the Claude reminder keep still; it was measured against the real binary, since neither a fixture nor documentation of it existed in this repository.
podsafety.Apply's state directory and error return were vestigial once the overlay went; both are gone, and --pod-safety no longer requires LEGION_STATE_DIR to write an overlay it never writes.

One has run and found a defect in its own predicate, fixed here; the other stopped at its input check.

The three migrations are 0065, 0066 and 0067, not 0062, 0063 and 0064: main landed those three numbers while this branch was open.

packages/claude-envoy/legion/ and dist/ are not regenerated here, as packages/claude-envoy/AGENTS.md requires; main's rebuild workflow writes them after the merge. scripts/build.ts carries the hook entry's change, and the plugin check in the tests builds a fresh tree.
openQuestions: A lost prompt_result from a live agent leaves a confirmed delivery unretired until that claim dies, is suspended or is retired; there is no timer backstop. Oh My Pi's protocol gives exactly one completion per accepted prompt, so this needs a dropped frame — a connection that closed and whose shim backlog overflowed before it redialled. The code before this change had the opposite failure for the same loss: it retired the task as served. A timer kind was judged not worth the table rows; the architect may decide otherwise.
discoveredComplexity: Nothing stops the outgoing role's running turn from writing the shared working copy once its phase ends. The approved spec decided this is text, not a mechanism, and both the phase-ended message and the worker prompt now carry it.

The forward merge was needed: GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING. Seven files conflicted, the branch's diff changed, so this head needs a full test round rather than a bare re-check. The fingerprints and every resolution are on the pull request.

In this pod `internal/testpg`'s teardown fails one random test per run with `drop test database: ERROR: permission denied to terminate process (SQLSTATE 42501)`, because the role lacks pg_signal_backend; every such failure named here passed when re-run alone. `internal/runtime/tmux`'s TestNewRefusesLaunchersItCannotRun needs tmux on a fixed PATH this pod has not got. The nine internal/daemon tests docs/solutions/testing/…INFRA-388.md names were skipped as that document says.

At the branch's base commit, 16 tests of packages/claude-envoy/tests/answers-hook.test.ts fail because the committed dist/session-hook.js predates the `answers` mode its src/ gained; main's rebuild workflow has since written it, and the forward merge brought that fix in.

Round 2 answers the tester's two failures. The head carried no CI because GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING and so built no merge ref: main had moved again, and had adopted a semantic-line-breaks layout for its guides, rewriting several tables as lists. Four prose files conflicted (AGENTS.md, docs/kubernetes.md, scripts/e2e/README.md, skills/AGENTS.md); each was resolved by taking main's version whole and re-applying this change's own edits into main's new shape. GitHub now reports MERGEABLE. One clause the re-application fixed beyond the merge: scripts/e2e/README.md's Stage 4a pod-baseline check still said the overlay is mode 444 and that `omp config get` reads bash.autoBackground.enabled as false, both of which describe the overlay this change deletes and which runtime/sandbox/live_operator_test.go had already dropped.

A2's first two sentences had no test, which the plan's departures did not cover, so the regression lock was missing rather than the behaviour. The case added in round 2 cost two traps worth recording: deep-worker declares model ["@deep"], a role writeStandinProfile does not map, so without a modelRoles entry the subagent dies in under a second with `No model selected` while the parent still reports the job complete — a false green for any case that checks the parent alone; and the subagent's own model request must be told from the parent's by deep-worker's system prompt, never by request order, since the host also sends label, self-check and skill routing-hint requests. The parent's first agent_end also carries isTerminal false while the job is pending, so a wait filtered on that flag never fires.

Two pod replacements during this issue lost unpushed work. The second lost a commit that had never been pushed, and the operator's rescue branch carried only the working copy's edits, so the A2 test had to be written twice. Every round now pushes to legion/INFRA-338 as soon as a commit exists.
